en: The expression μαϑητεύσατε βαπτίζοντες is therefore of deep significance. — “All power in heaven and on earth has been given to me” (so Jesus speaks in John

13, 31 of his glorification at the moment when Judas had left the company in order to betray Jesus to the Jews — at the point in time when he was looking toward the homecoming to his Father, who is greater than he; here, where he is presented as already withdrawn from everything that the world could demand of him, where it could have a part in him) — “All power has been given to me, in heaven and on earth; therefore go out into all peoples, and your making of disciples shall be that you initiate them into the relation of the Father, of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, so that it [they] may flow around and encompass them, as the water does the one dipped in water, in all points of their being — and see, I am with you the whole of the days until the consummation of the world.”
At this point in time, where Jesus is presented as removed from all actuality and personality, one can least of all think of an individuality, a personality of his being.
He is with them, whose being is permeated by the divine Spirit, who are initiated into the divine, whose being is alive in the divine, which is now consummated in him.
zh: 所以 μαϑητεύσατε βαπτίζοντες 这个说法含义很深。——“天上地下所有的权柄都赐给我了”（耶稣在《约翰福音》里这样说

13, 31，说的是他得荣耀，那是在犹大离开这一伙人、要把耶稣出卖给犹太人的那一刻，——在那个时刻，他正盼着回到比他更大的父那里去；而这里所表象的他，已经从世界可能向他要求的一切、从世界可能与他有份的一切中抽身而出），——“天上地下所有的权柄都赐给我了；所以你们要到万民中去，而你们使人作门徒，就是把他们引入父、子和神圣的精神的关系，让它〔他们〕像水对待那浸入水中的人一样，在他们本质的每一点上环绕他们、抚遍他们——看哪，我与你们同在，度过所有的日子，直到世界的成全。”
在这个时刻，耶稣被表现得超脱了一切现实性和人格性，最不能去设想的就是他的本质还有什么个体性、什么人格性。
他与他们同在——他们的本质被神性的精神渗透，他们被引入神性之中，他们的本质就在那如今在他身上得以圆满的神性里活着。

en: The immersion into the relation of the Father, the Son and the Spirit Luke expresses much more weakly (Luke

24, 47) than as a proclamation in the name of the Christ — of the change of mind and the release of sins; a proclamation that should begin in Jerusalem; they were witnesses of what had happened, he would send them the promise of his Father, and they should not begin their work outside Jerusalem until they were clothed with the power from on high. — A mere doctrine can be proclaimed and supported by the testimony of things that have happened, without its own Holy Spirit; but such a teaching would be no consecration, no immersion of the Spirit.

In Mark — if the last chapter were not quite genuine, his tone is still characteristic — this farewell of Jesus is expressed much more objectively; the spiritual appears in it more as an ordinary formula, the expressions [are] customary words grown cold through the habit of a church: proclaim the gospel (without further addition, a kind of terminus technicus), the believer and the baptized will be saved, the unbeliever will be condemned — the believer and the baptized already have the look of certain soulless words serving a sect or congregation as a badge, whose full concepts are presupposed.

Instead of the spirited [word]: I am with you all days, the being-filled of the believers with the Spirit of God and of the glorified Jesus, Mark speaks drily — without its being lifted up by enthusiasm and breathing with spirit — of wonderful mastery over actuality, of casting out devils and similar actions that the believers will be capable of, as objectively as one can speak of actions without mentioning their soul.
zh: 浸入父、子和精神的关系这件事，路加表达得弱得多（Luk.
24, 47），他只把它说成奉基督之名的宣讲——宣讲悔改和罪的赦免；这宣讲应当从耶路撒冷开始；他们是所发生之事的见证人，他要把父的应许差给他们，而他们不可在耶路撒冷之外先开始自己的工作，直到他们披上从上头来的能力。——单纯的学说可以宣讲，也可以靠已发生之事的见证来支撑，并不需要自己特有的神圣的精神；但这样的教导就不是祝圣，不是精神的浸入。
在《马可福音》里——即使最后一章并不完全可靠，它的调子也仍然很有特征——耶稣这场告别表达得客观得多；精神性的东西在它那里更像是普通的套语，那些说法〔是〕被一个教会的习惯弄冷了的常用词：传福音（没有进一步的补充，一种 terminus technicus），信而受洗的必得救，不信的必被定罪，——信而受洗的人已经有了某些没有灵魂的、充当教派或教团标记的说法的那副样子，这些说法的完整概念是被预设了的。
与那句有精神的话——我天天与你们同在——与信徒被上帝的精神、被得荣耀的耶稣所充满相反，马可却干巴巴地讲——既没有因热忱而被提升，也没有精神吹拂——讲对现实性的奇妙支配，讲赶鬼和诸如此类信徒将能做到的行为，讲得尽可能客观，就像人可以不提行为的灵魂而谈论行为那样客观。

en: The development of the divine in human beings, the relation into which they enter with God through being filled with the Holy Spirit, to become his sons and to live in the harmony of their whole being and character, of their developed manifoldness — a harmony in which not [only] their many-sided consciousness rings together into one spirit, the many shapes of life into one life, but through which also the dividing walls against other godlike beings are sublated and the same living spirit animates the different beings, which are therefore no longer merely alike but at one, do not form an assembly but a congregation, because they are united not in a universal, a concept, say as believers, but through life, through love — this living harmony of human beings, their community in God, Jesus calls the kingdom of God. — The Jewish language gave him the word kingdom, which brings something heterogeneous into the expression of the divine union of human beings, since it designates only a unity through ruling, through the power of a foreign element over a foreign element, which must be entirely removed from the beauty and the divine life of a pure human bond — the freest thing that is possible.

This idea of a kingdom of God completes and embraces the whole of the religion as Jesus founded it, and it remains to be considered whether it perfectly satisfies nature, or what need drove his disciples to something further.

In the kingdom of God the common element is that all are alive in God, not the common element in a concept, but love, a living bond that unites the believers, this feeling of the oneness of life, in which all oppositions, as such enmities, and also the unions of existing oppositions, — rights — are sublated; a new commandment I give you, says Jesus, that you love one another, by this one shall know that you are my disciples.
This friendship of souls, expressed as essence, as spirit for reflection, is the divine spirit, God, who rules the congregation.

Is there a more beautiful idea than a people of human beings related to one another through love? a more elevating one than to belong to a whole that as a whole, as one, is the Spirit of God — whose sons the individuals are?

Should there still be an incompleteness in this idea, that a fate would have power in it? or would this fate be the Nemesis that raged against too beautiful a striving, against a leaping over of nature?
zh: 神性在人里面的发展，以及他们因充满神圣的精神而与上帝进入的那种关系——成为他的儿子，并且在他们整个本质和性格、在他们已发展出来的杂多的和谐中生活，一种和谐：在其中，不〔只〕是他们多方面的意识汇入一个精神、众多生命形态汇入一个生命，而且通过它，与别的类似神的存在者之间的隔墙也被扬弃，同一个活的精神赋予这些不同的存在者以灵魂，于是他们不再只是相同，而是合一的，不是凑成一个集会，而是一个教团，因为他们不是在一个普遍者、一个概念里——比如作为信徒——而是在生命里、在爱里结合起来，——人这种活的和谐，他们在上帝中的共同体，耶稣称之为上帝之国。——犹太语言把“王国”这个词给了他，这个词把某种异质的东西带进了对人的神圣结合的表达，因为它表示的只是一种通过统治、通过一个外来者对另一个外来者的强力而来的统一，这种统一必须完全从一种纯粹人类结合的美和神圣生命中排除出去——那是可能的东西中最自由的东西。
上帝之国这个观念完成并包含了耶稣所创立的宗教的整体，接下来还要看，它是否完全满足了本性，或者说，是哪种需要把他的门徒逼向了更远的东西。
在上帝之国里，共同的东西就是所有人在上帝里面活着，不是在一个概念里的共同，而是爱，是一条把信徒联合起来的活的纽带，是这种生命合一的感受，在其中一切对立，作为对立也就是敌意，以及现存对立之间的种种结合，——权利——都被扬弃了；我给你们一条新的诫命，耶稣说，你们要彼此相爱，人们由此就可以认出你们是我的门徒。
这种灵魂的友谊，被表述为本质、表述为对反思而言的精神，就是神性的精神，就是上帝，是它统治着教团。
还有比一群通过爱而相互关联的人更美的观念吗？还有比属于这样一个整体更令人提升的观念吗——它作为整体、作为一，就是上帝的精神，而各个个人就是它的儿子？
难道这个观念里还留有不完满，竟会有一种命运在它里面拥有权力？或者，这命运就是那位复仇女神，她会向过于美的追求、向跨越本性的举动肆虐？

en: In love the human being has found himself again in another; because it is a union of life, it presupposed separation, a development, a cultivated many-sidedness of the same; and the more shapes life is alive in, the more points it can unite and feel itself in, the more inward love can be; the more extended in manifoldness the relations and feelings of the lovers are, the more inwardly love concentrates itself, the more exclusive it is, the more indifferent toward other forms of life; its joy mingles with every other life, acknowledges it, but withdraws at the feeling of an individuality; and the more isolated human beings stand in regard to their formation and their interest, [in] their relation to the world, the more peculiar each one has, the more limited love becomes to itself; and in order to have the consciousness of its happiness, in order to give it to itself, as it likes to do, it is necessary that it isolate itself, that it even create enmities for itself.

A love among many therefore admits only a certain degree of strength, of inwardness, and demands equality of spirit, of interest, of many relations of life, diminution of individualities; but this commonness of life, this equality of spirit, since it is not love, can come to consciousness only through its definite, strongly marked expressions; of an agreement in knowledge, in the same opinions, there can be no question; the union of many rests on the same need, it presents itself in objects that can be common, in relations that arise over them, and then in the common striving for the same things and in common activity and action; it can attach itself to a thousand objects of common possession and enjoyment and equal formation and recognize itself in them.

A multitude of the same purposes, the whole scope of physical need can be the object of united activity; in this the same spirit [presents itself], and this common spirit then also takes pleasure in making itself known in repose, in being glad of its union, in that it enjoys itself in joy and at play.

The friends of Jesus held together after his death, ate and drank in common, some of their brotherhoods abolished all property right among one another, others partly so, in abundant alms and contributions to the congregation; they spoke together of their departed friend and master, prayed in common and strengthened one another in faith and courage; their enemies accused some of their societies also of community of women; an accusation that they either did not have the courage and the purity to deserve, or were not ashamed of.
In common many went out to make other peoples partakers of their faith and their hopes; and because this is the only doing of the Christian congregation, proselytism is essentially proper to it.

Apart from this common enjoying, praying, eating, rejoicing, believing and hoping, apart from the single activity for the spreading of the faith, the enlargement of the commonness of devotion, there still lies a monstrous field of objectivity, which a fate of the most many-sided scope and mighty power sets up and which calls for manifold activity.
In the task of love the congregation disdains every union that would not be the most inward, every spirit that would not be the highest.

Not to mention the unnaturalness and insipidity of the splendid idea of a universal love of mankind, since it is not the striving of the congregation, the congregation must stop at love itself; apart from the relation of common faith and the presentations of this community in religious actions referring to it, every other connection in something objective, for a purpose, [for] a development of another side of life, for a common activity, every spirit of the congregation cooperating toward something other than the spreading of the faith and presenting itself and rejoicing in itself in other modifications and partial shapes of life, in games, is foreign to the congregation, it would not recognize itself in it, it would have departed from love, its only spirit, would have become unfaithful to its God; it would also not merely have left love but would have destroyed it too; for the members run the danger of colliding with one another with their individualities, and would have to do so all the more since their formation was [different] and they would thereby enter the domain of their different characters, the power of their different fates, and out of an interest in something slight, out of a different determinacy in something small, love would turn into hatred and an apostasy from God would follow.
This danger is averted only by an inactive, undeveloped love, in that it, the highest life, remains unliving.
Thus the unnatural extension of the scope of love entangles it in a contradiction, in a false striving that had to become the father of the most terrible suffering or active fanaticism.

This limitation of love to itself, its flight from all forms, even if its spirit already breathed in them or they sprang from it, this removal from all fate is precisely its greatest fate, and here is the point where Jesus is connected with fate, and indeed in the most sublime way, but suffered from it.
zh: 在爱里面，人已经在另一个人身上重新找到了自己；因为爱是生命的结合，它就预设了分离、一种发展、同一种生命已经教养出来的多面性；生命活得越是有更多形态，它就越能在更多的点上结合起来并感受到自己，爱也就越内在；相爱者的关系和感受在杂多上越是展开，爱越是内在地集中，它就越排他，对别的生命形式就越无所谓；它的快乐会与每一种别的生命相混合，承认它，但一感到有个体性就退回来；而人在教养和利益上、在〔与〕世界的关系上越是孤立，每个人拥有的独特之处越多，爱就越是被限制在自身之内；而为了拥有对自己幸福的意识，为了像它乐意做的那样把幸福给予自己，它就必须把自己隔离开来，甚至为自己造出敌意。

因此，许多人之间的爱只容许一定程度的强度、一定程度的深挚，它要求精神、利益、许多生活关系的相同，要求个体性的减少；但这种生命的共同性、这种精神的相同，既然不是爱，就只能通过它那些确定的、刻画鲜明的表现而进入意识；至于在认识上、在相同意见上的一致，根本谈不上；许多人的联结基于相同的困苦，它表现在可以共有的对象上、表现在由此产生的关系上，然后表现在对同样东西的共同追求以及共同的活动和行动上；它可以依附于千百个共同占有、共同享受、相同教养的对象，并在其中认出自己。
许多相同的目标、物质需要的整个范围，都可以成为联合活动的对象；在这种活动里，相同的精神〔表现出来〕，而这种共同的精神也乐于在安宁中让人认识自己，乐于为自己的结合而高兴，在欢乐中、在游戏中享受自己。
耶稣的朋友在他死后聚在一起，共同吃喝，他们的一些兄弟会取消了彼此之间的一切财产权，另一些只是部分地取消，办法是丰厚的施舍和给教团的捐款；他们一起谈论他们已离去的朋友和老师，共同祈祷，在信仰和勇气上互相坚固；他们的敌人还指责他们的一些团体共妻；这项指控，他们要么没有勇气和纯洁去配得上，要么并不为它感到羞耻。
许多人一起走出去，要让别的民族分享他们的信仰和希望；因为这是基督教教团唯一的行动，所以劝人入教本质上是它固有的。
除了这种共同的享受、祈祷、吃喝、欢乐、信仰和希望，除了为传播信仰、扩大敬虔的共同性这一唯一的活动之外，还摊着一片巨大的客观性领域，一种范围极为多方面、威力强大的命运把它摆在那里，并要求人多方面地行动。
在爱这项任务里，教团鄙视任何不是最内在的结合，鄙视任何不是最高的精神。

且不说普遍的人类爱那个华丽观念有多不自然、多乏味——因为它并不是教团的追求——教团必须停留在爱本身；除了共同信仰的关系以及这种共同体在与之相关的宗教行动中的表现之外，任何别的联系——落在某种客观的东西里、为了一个目的、〔为了〕生命另一面的发展、为了共同的活动——任何为传播信仰之外的其他东西共同出力、并在生命中别的变形和局部形态中、在游戏中表现出来并为此欣喜的教团精神，对教团来说都是陌生的，它不会在其中认出自己，它就是已经离开了爱、离开了它唯一的精神，就是已经对自己的上帝不忠了；而且它不只是离开了爱，还会把爱毁掉；因为成员们有以各自的个体性互相撞上的危险，而且他们不得不更加如此，因为他们的教养〔各不相同〕，他们就由此进入各自不同性格的领域、各自不同命运的力量之中，于是会因为对微末之事的兴趣、因为在小事上的不同规定，使爱变成恨，接着就是对上帝的背离。
这种危险只有靠一种不活动、未发展的爱才能避开，也就是让这最高的生命毫无生气地待着。
于是，爱在范围上不自然的扩展把它缠进一种矛盾、一种错误的追求，而这种追求必然会成为最可怕的那种或忍受、或行动的狂热的父亲。
爱这样限制在自身之内，这样逃避一切形式——即使它的精神早已在这些形式中吹拂，或者这些形式就是从它那里来的——这样远离一切命运，恰恰就是它最大的命运；而这里正是耶稣与命运相联结的那一点，而且是以最崇高的方式相联结，但他却因命运而受苦。

en: With the courage and the faith of a man inspired by God, whom clever people call an enthusiast, Jesus appeared among the Jewish people; he appeared anew in his own spirit, the world lay before him as it was to become, and the first relation in which he placed himself toward it was to call it to become other, he began by calling out to all: change, for the kingdom of God is near; had the spark of life slumbered in the Jews, it would have needed only one breath to flare up into flame, which would have burned all their miserable titles and claims; had there lain in them, with their restlessness and dissatisfaction with actuality, the need for something purer, the call of Jesus would have found faith, and this faith would have brought the believed into existence in the same moment.
With their faith the kingdom of God would have been present.

Jesus would really have only expressed to them what lay undeveloped and unconscious in their heart; and with the finding of the word, with the coming-to-consciousness of the need, the bonds would have fallen away, from the old fate only twitchings of the dead life would still have stirred, and the new would have stood there.
But so the Jews did want something other than what had been hitherto; but they pleased themselves too much in the pride of their servitude to find what they sought in what Jesus offered them.

Their counter-action, the answer that their genius gave to the call of Jesus, was a very impure attention; a few pure souls attached themselves to him with the drive to be formed; with great good nature, with the faith of a pure enthusiast, he took their longing for a satisfied disposition, their drive for completion, their renunciation of some former relations, which were mostly not splendid, for freedom and healed or conquered fate; for soon after his acquaintance with them he held them capable and his people ripe to follow a more widely spread proclamation of the kingdom of God, he sent his disciples in pairs around the land, to let his call resound multiplied, but the divine spirit did not speak in their preaching, after much longer intercourse they still so often let a small, at least unpurified soul show through, of which only a few branches had been penetrated by the divine.
Their whole instruction, apart from the negative that it contains, was to proclaim the nearness of the kingdom of God.
They soon gather again to Jesus, and one sees no effect of the hope of Jesus and of their apostolizing.

The indifference of the reception of his call soon turned into hatred against him, whose effect on him was an ever-rising bitterness against his age and his people, chiefly against those in whom the spirit of his nation dwelt most strongly and most passionately, against the Pharisees and the leaders of the people; his tone toward them is no attempt to reconcile them with himself, to affect their spirit, but the most violent outbursts of his bitterness against them, the unveiling of their spirit hostile to him; he does not deal with this spirit even with the faith in the possibility of a change.

If their whole character resisted him, then on occasions of speaking with them about religious subjects he could not set out upon a refutation and an instruction; he silences them only by argumenta ad hominem, the true opposed to them he addresses to the other people present.
As it seems after the return of his disciples to him (Matth.

11) he renounces his people and has felt (v. 25) that God reveals himself only to the simple; and from now on he restricts himself to activity upon individuals; and lets the fate of his nation stand untouched, in that he separates himself from it and tears his friends away from it; to the extent that Jesus does not see the world changed, to that extent he flees it and all relations with it; to the extent that he collides with the whole fate of his people, he behaves, even if his behavior seems contradictory to him, passively toward it.

Give to Caesar what is Caesar's, he says, when the Jews brought up against him the side of their fate, to be tributary to the Romans; when it seemed contradictory to him that he and his friends should also pay the tribute that was laid on the Jews, he told Peter to pay it, in order to give no offense.

He stood with the state in the single relation of dwelling within its jurisdiction, and to the consequence of this power over him he submitted himself with contradiction of his spirit, suffering with consciousness.
The kingdom of God is not of this world; only for it there is a great difference whether this world is present as opposed to it or does not exist, is only possible.

Since the former was the case and Jesus suffered from the state with consciousness, so with this relation to the state a great side of living union is already cut off, for the members of the kingdom of God an important bond, a part of freedom, of the negative character of a union of beauty, a multitude of active relations, living connections, are lost; the citizens of the kingdom of God become private persons opposed to a hostile state, excluding themselves from it.

This limitation of life appears, moreover, more as the violence of an alien ruling power over external things, which can themselves be given up with freedom, than as a robbery of life - for those who were never active in such a union, never enjoyed this bond and this freedom, especially when the civil relation chiefly concerns only property.
What is lost in multitude of relations, in manifoldness of joyful and beautiful bonds, is replaced by gain in isolated individuality and the narrow-minded consciousness of peculiarities.

From the idea of the kingdom of God all relations founded by a state are indeed excluded, which stand infinitely lower than the living relations of the divine bond and can only be despised by such a bond, but if it was present and Jesus or the community could not sublate it, then the fate of Jesus and of his community remaining faithful to him in this remains a loss of freedom, a limitation of life, a passivity in the being-ruled by an alien power that one despises, but which nevertheless left him unmixed the little that Jesus needed from it, existence among his people. - Apart from this side of life, which can rather be called not life but only possibility of life, the [Jewish] spirit had not only taken possession of all modifications of life, but had also made itself in them into law as state and crippled the purest, most immediate forms of nature into determinate legalities.

In the kingdom of God there can be no relation except that which proceeds from the most ruthless love and thereby the highest freedom, which receives from beauty alone the form of its appearance and its relation to the world.

Because of the impurity of life Jesus could carry the kingdom of God only in his heart, could enter into relation with human beings only in order to form them, in order to develop the good spirit that he believed in them, - in order first to create human beings whose world would be his; but in his actual world he had to flee all living relations, because all lay under the law of death, human beings were caught under the power of the Jewish; through a relation free on both sides he would have entered into a bond with the web of Jewish legalities, and in order not to desecrate or tear apart a relation entered into, he would have had to let himself be entangled by its threads, and so he could find freedom only in emptiness, because every modification of life was bound; therefore Jesus isolated himself from his mother, his brothers and relatives; he was not allowed to love a woman, not to beget children, not to become a father of a family, not to become a fellow citizen who enjoyed living together with the others.

The fate of Jesus was to suffer from the fate of his nation, either to make it his own and bear its necessity and share its enjoyment and unite his spirit with its spirit, but to sacrifice his beauty, his connection with the divine, - or to thrust the fate of his people away from himself, but to preserve his life undeveloped and unenjoyed within himself; in neither case to fulfill nature: in the former to feel only fragments of it, and even these impure; in the latter to bring it fully to consciousness, but to recognize its form only as a shining shadow whose essence is the highest truth, yet to renounce the feeling of it, its animation in deed and actuality.
Jesus chose the latter fate, the separation of his nature and the world, and demanded the same of his friends: "whoever loves father or mother, son or daughter more than me, is not worthy of me".

But the deeper he felt this separation, the less he could bear it calmly, and his activity was the courageous reaction of his nature against the world; and his struggle was pure and sublime, because he had recognized fate in its whole extent and set himself opposite to it.

His and his community's resistance, founded by him, to the corruption had to bring this corruption to consciousness of itself and to the spirit still freer than it, and to divide its fate against itself; the struggle of the pure with the impure is a sublime sight, but it soon changes into a horrible one when the holy itself has suffered from the unholy and when the two are fused together, with the presumption of being pure, rages against fate, while it itself still lies caught under it.

Jesus foresaw the whole horror of this derangement; I came not, he said, to bring peace to the earth, but the sword; I came to divide the son against his father, the daughter against her mother, the bride against her mother-in-law.

What has partly renounced fate, but partly stands in league with it, with or without consciousness of this mixture, must tear itself and nature apart all the more terribly, and in the mixture of nature and unnaturalness the attack upon the latter must also strike the former, the wheat be trampled with the tares and the holiest of nature itself be violated, because it is interwoven with the unholy.

With the consequences before his eyes, Jesus did not think of holding back his activity, in order to spare the world its fate, to soften its convulsions and to leave it in its downfall the comforting faith in guiltlessness.
zh: 耶稣带着一个为神所鼓舞的男子的勇气和信仰，出现在犹太民族中间——这种人在聪明人嘴里被叫做狂热者；他是凭着自己的精神重新出场的，世界躺在他面前，是它应当变成的样子，而他为自己同世界建立的第一层关系，就是召唤它变成另一个样子：他一开口就向所有人喊：改吧，因为上帝之国近了；假如犹太人心里还睡着一点生命的火星，那只需要一口气，就能燃成火焰，把他们那些可怜的头衔和要求统统烧掉；假如在他们的不安、他们对现实的不满里，本来就藏着对更纯净之物的需要，那么耶稣的这一声召唤就会找到信仰，而这信仰会在同一瞬间把所信的东西带进定在。
有他们的信仰，上帝之国就已经在了。
耶稣其实只是把他们心里未展开、无意识地放着的东西说了出来；而一旦找到了这个词，一旦这需要进入意识，那些束缚就会脱落，从旧命运那里只会还剩下一丝死去的生命的抽搐，而新的东西就会立在那里。
可是实际情形是，犹太人虽然想要跟以往不同的东西，但他们太安于自己受奴役的那份骄傲，不肯在他们所寻找的东西里认出耶稣向他们提供的东西。

他们的反作用，他们的天才对耶稣的召唤所给出的回答，是一种很不纯净的注意；少数几个纯净的灵魂带着受教养的冲动依附了他；他怀着极大的善良，怀着一位纯净的狂热者的信仰，把他们的渴望当成已满足的心意，把他们的冲动当成完成，把他们放弃某些旧有关系（这些关系多半并不光鲜）当成自由和已治愈或已被战胜的命运；因为同他们相识不久，他就认为他们有能力、他的民族也已成熟，可以听从一次传播得更广的上帝之国的宣告，于是他派门徒两人一组走遍各地，好让他的召唤被复制着响开去，但神圣的精神并没有在他们的布道中说话，相处久得多之后，他们还是常常露出一个狭小的、至少是未洗净的灵魂，神圣的东西只渗透了它的少数枝杈。
他们所受的全部教导，除了其中包含的否定的一面之外，就是宣告上帝之国近了。
他们很快又聚回耶稣身边，而人们看不到耶稣的希望和他们的使徒工作有什么效果。
对他这声召唤的冷淡接待，很快就变成了对他的仇恨，这仇恨在他身上起的作用，是对他的时代和他的民族越来越高的恼怒，尤其是对那些他的民族的精神住得最强、最热烈的人，对法利赛人和民众的领袖；他对他们说话的语气，不是要同他们和解、要触动他们精神的尝试，而是他的恼怒对他们最激烈的爆发，是对他们那股敌视他的精神的揭露；他对待这种精神，甚至不带着对改变之可能性的信仰。
既然他们的整个品性都抵抗他，那么他在有机会同他们谈宗教题目时，就不可能去反驳和教导；他只用 argumenta ad hominem 让他们闭嘴，而与他们相对立的真理，他是讲给在场的其他人听的。
照他的门徒回到他身边之后的情形看（Matth.
11），他放弃了自己的民族，并且已经感到（V. 25），上帝只向单纯的人启示自己；从这时起他把自己限于对个人的作用；他让他的民族的命运原封不动地立在那里，办法是把自己从它里面分出去，并把他的朋友们从它那里夺出来；耶稣看不到世界被改变到什么程度，他就逃离世界到什么程度，逃离同它的一切关系；他同他民族的整个命运相撞到什么程度，他就对它采取被动的态度到什么程度，哪怕他的这种态度在他看来是自相矛盾的。
当犹太人把他们的命运中向罗马人纳贡的那一面拿到他面前来说时，他说：该撒的归该撒；当在他看来，他和他的朋友们也要缴纳加在犹太人身上的贡赋是自相矛盾的时候，为了不引起冒犯，他叫彼得去缴。
他同国家只处在一种关系里：待在国家管辖的范围之内；而对于这种权力凌驾于他的后果，他是带着自己精神的反抗、带着意识的受苦而顺从的。
上帝之国不是属于这个世界的；不过对它来说，这个世界的不同很大：这个世界是作为对立的东西存在着，还是根本不存在、只是可能。
既然情形是前者，耶稣又是带着意识从国家那里受苦，那么单是这层同国家的关系，就已经切掉了一大片活的结合，对上帝之国的成员来说，一条重要的纽带被割断了，一部分自由、一个美的同盟的否定性格的一部分、一大堆起作用的关系和活的联系都失去了；上帝之国的公民变成了同敌对国家相对立、把自己从这个国家排除出去的私人。
这种生命上的限制，此外更多表现为一种异己的统治力量对外部事物的暴力——这些外部事物本身是可以带着自由放弃的——而不表现为对生命的掠夺：这是对那些从未在这种结合中起过作用、从未享受过这种同盟和这种自由的人来说的，尤其是当市民关系主要只涉及财产的时候。
在关系的数量上、在欢乐而美好的纽带的多彩上失去的东西，靠孤立个体性的收获和对自己那些独特之处的狭窄意识补了回来。

从上帝之国的观念看，由一个国家所建立的一切关系固然都被排除在外，这些关系比神圣同盟的那些活的关系无限地低下，只能被这样一种同盟蔑视；但假如它已经存在，而耶稣或教团又不能扬弃它，那么耶稣以及在这方面忠于他的教团的命运，就仍然是一种自由上的损失，一种生命上的限制，一种在受异己力量支配中的被动——这力量人们蔑视，可它毕竟把耶稣从它那里需要的那一点点东西，即在他的民族中间的存在，不加混杂地让给了他。——除了生命的这一面（这一面更该叫做不是生命，而只是生命的可能性），[犹太]精神不但在生命的一切形态变化中占有了生命，而且在其中把自己弄成了作为国家的法律，把自然最纯净、最直接的形态弄残成了确定的法律条文。
在上帝之国里不可能有任何关系，除了那种从最不顾及的爱、因而从最高的自由中产生出来的关系，它单从美那里得到自己现象的形状和它同世界的关系。

由于生命的受污染，耶稣只能把上帝之国放在心里，只能同人发生关系，为的是教养他们，为的是发展他在他们身上所信的那个善的精神，——为的是先造出人来，让这些人的世界成为他的世界；但在他现实的世界里，他必须逃避一切活的关系，因为一切都在死亡的法则之下，人都被犹太的东西的力量困住；通过一种双方都自由的关系，他就会进入同犹太律法条文那套织物的同盟，而为了不把已经结成的关系亵渎掉或撕断，他就得让自己被它的线缠住，于是他只能到空无中去寻找自由，因为生命的每一种形态变化都被束缚着；所以耶稣把自己从他的母亲、他的兄弟和亲属那里孤立出来；他不可以爱女人，不可以生孩子，不可以做家长，不可以做同别人一起享受共同生活的同胞。

耶稣的命运，就是从自己民族的命运中受苦：要么把它变成自己的命运，承担它的必然性，分享它的享受，把自己的精神同它的精神结合起来，但这样一来就要牺牲他的美、他同神圣之物的联系，——要么把自己民族的命运从自己身上推开，但这样一来他的生命就在自身中保持着未展开、未被享受的状态；两种情形都不能把自然充实起来：在前一种情形里只能感受到它的碎片，而且连这些碎片也是受污染的；在后一种情形里虽然把它完整地带进意识，但只把它的形状认作一个发亮的影子、这影子的本质是最高的真理，却要放弃对它的感受、放弃它在行动和现实中的被激活。
耶稣选择了后一种命运，即他的自然同世界的分离，并且向他的朋友们也要求这一点：“谁爱父亲或母亲、儿子或女儿过于爱我，就不配做我的人”。
但他越是深切地感到这种分离，就越不能平静地承受它，而他的作为就是他的自然对世界的勇敢的反作用；他的斗争是纯净而崇高的，因为他已经认出了命运的全部范围，并把自己同它对立起来。
他和他所建立的教团对败坏的抵抗，必然把这种败坏带向对它自己、也对那种比它更自由的精神的意识，并让它的命运同自己分裂；纯净者同不纯净者的斗争是一幅崇高的景象，但它很快就会变成一幅可怖的景象，当神圣者自己也从不清净者那里受了苦，而两者的融合又带着纯净的僭妄向命运发怒，自己却还被困在命运之下的时候。
耶稣预见到了这种紊乱的全部可怖；他说，我来不是要给人间带来和平，而是要带来刀剑；我来是要让儿子同父亲分裂，让女儿同母亲分裂，让新娘同婆婆分裂。
那种一部分已经同命运断绝了关系、另一部分却还同它结着盟的东西，无论对这种混合有意识还是无意识，都必然更可怕地把自己和自然撕裂开来；而在自然和非自然的混合中，对后者的攻击也必然击中前者，麦子同稗子一起被践踏，连自然最神圣的东西本身也受到伤害，因为它已经缠进了不清净的东西里。
眼前放着这些后果，耶稣并没有想到要收回自己的作为，好让世界免去它的命运，让它的抽搐缓和下来，并在它的沉沦中留给它那份对无罪的安慰人心的信仰。

en: The existence of Jesus was therefore separation from the world and flight from it into heaven; restoration of the life that comes away empty, in ideality; at every thing that conflicted with him, remembrance and looking up to God; but in part activity of the divine and to that extent struggle with fate, partly in spreading the kingdom of God, with the presentation of which the whole kingdom of the world collapsed and vanished in itself; partly in immediate reaction against individual parts of fate, just as they happened to strike against him, — except against the part of fate that appeared immediately as the state and also came to consciousness in Jesus, toward which he behaved passively.
zh: 所以，耶稣的存在就是与世界的分离，是从世界逃到天上；是把空手而去的生命在观念性中恢复过来；面对每一个与他相争的东西，就回忆并仰望上帝；但一部分是对神性的施行，就此而言是与命运的争战——这一方面是在传播上帝之国，随着对这国的展示，整个世界的王国就在自身中崩塌、消失了；另一方面是对命运各个部分的直接反应，只要它们恰好撞到他身上——唯独对命运中直接作为国家出现、并且在耶稣身上也进入意识的那一部分例外，对之他采取的是被动的态度。

en: The fate of Jesus was not entirely the fate of his congregation, since it was something composed out of several, who indeed lived in the same separation from the world, but each member found several like-minded people, they held together and could keep themselves more distant from the world in actuality, and since thereby there was less of meeting and of striking against it, they were less provoked by it, lived less in the negative activity of struggle, and the need for positive life had to become greater in them, for commonness of the negative gives no enjoyment, is no beauty.
Sublation of property, introduced community of goods, common meals belong more to the negative of union than that it would be a positive union.

The essence of their covenant was setting apart from human beings and love among one another; the two are necessarily connected; this love was not to be and could not be a union of individualities, but the union in God, and in God alone; in faith only that can unite itself which sets an actuality over against itself, sets itself apart from it; thereby this opposition was fixed and became an essential part of the principle of the covenant; and love had to keep always the form of love, of faith in God, without becoming living and presenting itself in shapes of life, because every shape of life can be grasped by the understanding as capable of being set over against it, as its object, as an actuality; and the relation to the world had to become an anxiousness before its touches, a fear of every form of life, because in each, since it has shape and is only one side, its lack can be shown, and this lacking thing is a share in the world.
Thus the covenant of the congregation found no reconciliation of fate, but the opposite extreme of the Jewish spirit, not the middle of the extremes in beauty.

The Jewish spirit had fixed the modifications of nature, the relations of life, into actualities, but as gifts of the ruler he was not only not ashamed of their poverty, but rather his pride and his life was the possession of actualities.

The spirit of the Christian congregation likewise saw actualities in every relation of life as it develops and presents itself; but since, as the feeling of love, objectivity was the greatest enemy to it, it remained just as poor as the Jewish spirit, but it despised the wealth for whose sake the Jewish spirit served.
zh: 耶稣的命运并不完全是他的教团的命运，因为教团是由多个人组合成的东西，这些人虽然生活在与世界同样的分离之中，但每个成员都找得到几个与他同调的人，他们聚在一起，在现实性中也能与尘世保持更远的距离；而既然这样，与世界的相遇和碰撞就少了，他们被它刺激得也就少了，更少生活在斗争的否定性活动里，于是对肯定性生命的需要在他们身上必然变得更大，因为否定之物的共同性不给人享受，也不是美。
扬弃财产、实行财产公有、共同进餐，这些更多属于结合的否定面，而不是一种肯定的结合。

他们的盟约的本质，就是从人群中分离出来，以及彼此之间的爱；这两者必然相连；这种爱不应当是、也不可能是诸个体性的结合，而是在上帝之中的结合，而且只在上帝之中；在信仰里，能够结合起来的只有那种把一种现实性设定在自己对面、并从其中分离出来的东西；这样一来，这种对立就被固定下来，成了盟约原则的一个本质部分；而爱必须始终保持着爱的形式、对上帝的信仰的形式，不能成为活的，不能在生命的诸形态中把自己展示出来，因为每一种生命形态都可能被知性当作可以置于对面的东西、当作它的对象、当作一种现实性来把握；与世界的关联也必然变成对它每一次触碰的担惊受怕，变成对任何一种生命形式的恐惧，因为在每一种形态里——既然它有形态，而且只是一个侧面——都能显出它的欠缺，而这欠缺的东西就是对世界的一份参与。
所以，教团的盟约没有找到命运的和解，而是找到了犹太精神那相反的一端，不是诸极端在美之中的中项。
犹太精神把自然的诸变化、生命的诸关系都固定成了现实性，但作为统治者的赠礼，他非但不为它们的贫乏感到羞耻，反而他的骄傲和他的生命就在于占有这些现实性。
基督教教团的精神同样在生命发展和展示自己的每一重关系里看到现实性；但既然对它来说，作为爱的感受，客观性是最大的敌人，它就仍然和犹太精神一样贫乏，只不过它鄙弃那种财富，而犹太精神正是为了这财富才服役的。

en: Life-despising enthusiasm can very easily pass over into fanaticism; for in order to preserve itself in its relationlessness, it must destroy that by which it is destroyed and which, even if it is the purest, is impure for it, must injure its content, often the most beautiful relations.

Enthusiasts of later times have made the despising of all forms of life, because they are polluted, into an unconditional empty shapelessness and have declared war on every drive of nature merely because it seeks an outer form, and the more terrible was the effect of these attempted suicides, of this holding fast to the empty unity, the firmer the bond of manifoldness still was in their minds; for since there was in them only the consciousness of limited forms, nothing remained to them but a flight into the void brought about by atrocities and devastations — but when the fate of the world became too great and maintained itself alongside and within the church, which is incompatible with it, there was no longer any thought of flight.

Great hypocrites against nature have therefore attempted to find and to maintain an unnatural connection of the manifoldness of the world and of the lifeless unity, of all limited lawful relations and human virtues, with the simple spirit; they devised for every civil action or for every expression of pleasure and desire a hiding corner in the unity, in order thus through deception at once to preserve every limitation for themselves, to enjoy it, and at the same time to escape it.
zh: 蔑视生命的狂热很容易转为偏执；因为要在自己的毫无关联中维持自己，它就必须毁掉那个毁掉它的东西——那东西即便最纯净，对它来说也是不纯净的——必须伤害它的内容，往往还伤害最美好的那些关系。

后世那些狂热者把对一切生命形式的鄙弃——因为它们被玷污了——弄成了一种无条件的、空洞的无形态状态，并向自然的每一种冲动宣战，只因为它在寻求一种外在形式；而人心里的杂多之束缚还越牢固，这些尝试性的自杀、这种死守空洞统一的举动的后果就越可怕；因为在他们心里只有对受限制形式的意识，所以留给他们的就只剩下一条靠暴行和毁灭来完成的逃进空无的路——但当世界的命运变得太大，并且在教会旁边、在教会内部把自己维持下来——教会与它是不能相容的——这时就再也谈不上逃走了。
所以，那些对自然大行伪善的人就试图找到并维持一种反自然的联结，把世界的杂多和无生命的统一、把一切受限制的法律性关系和人的美德，同单纯的精神联结起来；他们为每一种市民行为，或者为每一次快乐和欲望的流露，都在统一里想出一个藏身的角落，好靠欺骗既把每一种限制为自己保留下来，又享受它，同时又躲开它。

en: Since Jesus disdained to live with the Jews, but at the same time always fought against their actualities with his ideal, it could not fail that he had to succumb among them; he did not avoid this development of his fate, but he certainly did not seek it out either; to every enthusiast who enthuses only for himself, death is welcome, but whoever enthuses for a great plan can leave the scene on which he was to develop only with pain; Jesus died with the confidence that his plan would not be lost.
zh: 既然耶稣不屑于和犹太人一起生活，却又始终以自己的理想去对抗他们的种种现实性，那就免不了，他必定要在他们中间倒下；他并没有回避自己命运的这一发展，但他当然也没有去寻求它；对每一个只为自己而狂热的狂热者来说，死是受欢迎的，可是为一个宏大计划而狂热的人，只能带着痛苦离开那个本该让他展开自己的舞台；耶稣死时怀着这样的确信：他的计划不会落空。

en: Over against the negative side of the fate of the Christian congregation, the opposition to the world that turns the modifications of life into determinacies and the relations with them therefore into crimes, stands the positive side, the bond of love.

Through the extension of love to a whole congregation there enters into its character that it is not a living union of individualities, but that its enjoyment is restricted to the mutual consciousness that they love one another — the fatednesslessness through flight into unfulfilled life was made easier for the members of the congregation by the fact that they formed a congregation that refrained from all forms of life in relation to one another, or determined them only through the general spirit of love, that is, did not live in these forms — this love is a divine spirit, but not yet religion; for it to become that, it had to present itself at the same time in an objective form; it, a feeling, a subjective thing, had to melt together with what is represented, the universal, and thereby gain the form of a being capable of being worshipped and worthy of worship.

This need, to unite the subjective and the objective, the feeling and its demand for objects, the understanding, through the imagination, in a beautiful thing, a god, this need, the highest of the human spirit, is the drive toward religion.

For this drive of the Christian congregation, faith in God could not be satisfaction; for in their god only their common feeling had to find itself; in the god of the world all beings are united; the members of the congregation are not so as such in him; their harmony is not the harmony of the whole, otherwise they would not form a particular congregation, otherwise they would not be bound to one another by love; the divinity of the world is not the presentation of their love, of their divine element.

Jesus's need for religion was satisfied in the god of the whole; for his looking up to him was each of his constant collisions with the world, his flight from it; he needed only the opposite of the world, in which his opposition itself was grounded; he was his father, he was one with him.

But with his congregation the constant collision with the world fell away more, it lived without active struggle against it and was to that extent happy not to be constantly provoked by it and therefore not to have to flee only to the opposite, to God; rather it found in its community, in its love an enjoyment, something real, a kind of living relation; but since every relation is opposed to that which is related, and the feeling still has actuality, or, expressed subjectively, the capacity for it, the understanding, as something opposed to it, its lack had to be supplemented in something that unites both.

The congregation has the need of a god who is the god of the congregation, in which precisely the exclusive love, its character, its relation to one another is presented; not as a symbol or allegory, not as a personification of something subjective, in which one would be conscious of its separation from its presented [shape], but which is at the same time in the heart, at the same time feeling and object; feeling as spirit that breathes through all and remains one being, even if each individual becomes conscious of his feeling as his individual one.
zh: 基督教教团命运的否定面，即那种把生命的诸变化弄成种种规定性、从而把与它们的关系弄成罪行的对世界的对立，与之相对的是肯定面，即爱的纽带。

由于爱扩展到了整个教团，它的性格里就带上了这样一点：它不是诸个体性的活的结合，而是它的享受只限于彼此意识到自己在相爱——通过逃进未实现的生命而达到的无命运性，对教团成员来说之所以比较容易，是因为他们构成了一个教团，这个教团在彼此之间对一切生命形式都有所节制，或者只通过爱的普遍精神来规定它们，也就是说，并不生活在这些形式里——这种爱是一种神性的精神，但还不是宗教；要成为宗教，它就必须同时以一种客观的形式把自己展示出来；它作为一种感受、一种主观的东西，必须与那被表象的东西、与普遍的东西融汇在一起，从而获得一个可被崇拜、配得上崇拜的本质的形式。
这种需要，即把主观的东西和客观的东西、把感受以及感受对对象的要求、把知性，通过想象力在一个美的东西、一个神之中结合起来，这种需要，人的精神的最高需要，就是趋向宗教的冲动。
对基督教教团的这种冲动来说，对上帝的信仰不可能成为满足；因为在他们那个上帝里面，必定只能找到他们共同的感受；而世界的上帝里面，万物是结合着的；教团成员作为教团成员并不结合在他里面；他们的和谐不是整体的和谐，否则他们就不构成一个特殊的教团，否则他们就不会通过爱彼此结合；世界的神性并不是他们的爱、他们的神性的展示。
耶稣对宗教的需要，在整体的上帝里面得到了满足；因为他对上帝的仰望，就是他与世界的每一次不断碰撞，就是他对世界的逃离；他所需要的只是那与世界相对立的东西，而他的对立本身正是建立在这东西之中；上帝是他的父亲，他与上帝是一体的。

但在他的教团那里，与世界不断的碰撞就在更大程度上消失了，它活着而没有对世界展开行动上的斗争，就此而言它是幸运的：不必不断受它刺激，因此也不必只逃向那对立的东西、逃向上帝；相反，它在自己的共同体中、在自己的爱里找到了一种享受，一种真实的东西，一种活的关联；只是，既然每一种关系都与被关系者相对立，感受也还有现实性，或者用主观的方式说，还有感受的能力即知性作为与它相对立的东西，所以它的欠缺必须在一种把两者结合起来的东西里得到补足。
教团需要的是一个上帝，这个上帝是教团的上帝，在这个上帝里面，恰恰是那种排他的爱、它的性格、他们彼此的关系得到了展示；不是作为一个象征或寓言，不是作为一种主观之物的拟人化——在那种拟人化那里，人会意识到它与它所展示的[形态]的分离——而是一个同时就在心里、同时既是感受又是对象的东西；这感受作为精神，贯穿所有人，并且始终是一个本质，即便每一个个别的人都意识到自己的感受是他个别的感受。

en: A circle of love, a circle of minds that give up their rights to everything particular in relation to one another and are united only through common faith and hope, whose enjoyment and joy is solely this pure concord of love, is a small kingdom of God; but their love is not religion, for the unity, the love of human beings, does not at the same time contain the presentation of this unity.
Love unites them, but the beloved do not recognize this union; where they do recognize, they recognize something separated.

For the divine to appear, the invisible spirit must be united with something visible, so that everything is in one, cognition and feeling, so that there is a complete synthesis, a perfected harmony, so that harmony and the harmonious are one.

Otherwise there remains, in relation to the whole of separable nature, a drive that is too small for the infinity of the world and too great for its objectivity and cannot be satiated; there remains the inextinguishable, unsatisfied drive toward God.
zh: 一个爱的圈子，一个由这样一些心组成的圈子：他们在彼此之间放弃对一切特殊之物的权利，只通过共同的信仰和希望结合在一起，他们的享受和快乐就只是爱这种纯粹的一致，——这样一个圈子就是一个小小的上帝之国；但他们的爱还不是宗教，因为这种一致，人的爱，并不同时包含对这种一致的展示。
爱把他们结合起来，但被爱的人们并不认识这种结合；他们有所认识的地方，认识到的都是分离出来的东西。
要使神性的东西显现出来，不可见的精神就必须与可见的东西结合起来，使一切都在一个之中，认识与感受都在一个之中，使有一种完全的综合、一种完成了的和谐，使和谐与和谐的东西是一个。
否则，在可分离的自然这个整体面前，就还留着一种冲动，它对世界的无限性来说太小，对世界的客观性来说又太大，并且无法被喂饱；那不可磨灭的、得不到满足的趋向上帝的冲动就还留在那里。

en: After the death of Jesus his disciples were like sheep that have no shepherd; a friend had died on them, but they had also hoped that he was the one who would free Israel (Luk.

24, 21), and this hope was gone with his death; he had taken everything with him into the grave; his spirit had not remained in them.125) — Their religion, their faith in pure life, had hung on the individual, Jesus; he was their living bond and the revealed, shaped divine, in him God had also appeared to them, his individual united for them the indeterminate of harmony and the determinate in one living being.
With his death they were thrown back into the separation of the visible and the invisible, of the spirit and the actual.

True, the remembrance of this divine being, but now far from them, would have remained to them; the violence that his dying exercised over them would in time have been broken in them, the dead man would not have remained a mere dead man to them, the pain over the moldering body would gradually have yielded to the contemplation of his divinity; and the incorruptible spirit and the image of a purer humanity would have come forth for them out of his grave; but alongside the veneration of this spirit, the enjoyment of contemplating this image, the remembrance of the life of this image would have stood, this sublime spirit would always have had its opposite in his vanished existence; and its presence before the imagination would have been bound up with a longing that would only have designated the need of religion, but the congregation would still have had no god of its own.
zh: 耶稣死后，他的门徒就像没有牧人的羊；他们死了一个朋友，可是他们本来还希望，他就是那位要解放以色列的人（Luk.
24, 21），而这个希望随着他的死也破灭了；他把一切都带进了坟墓；他的精神没有留在他们里面。125）——他们的宗教、他们对纯净生命的信仰，本来一直系在耶稣这个个体身上；他是他们活的纽带，是那被启示出来的、有形态的神性，在他们看来，上帝也在他里面显现过，他的个体把和谐的未规定者和规定者在一个活的东西里为他们结合了起来。
随着他的死，他们又被抛回了可见者与不可见者、精神与现实者的分离之中。

诚然，对这一个神性本质的怀念会留给他们，不过这怀念现在离他们很远了；他的死对他们所施加的暴力，本来会随着时间在他们身上被折断，死者对他们本来不会一直只是一个死者，对那正在腐烂的肉体的痛苦本来会渐渐让位于对他神性的直观；而那不会腐朽的精神和更纯净的人性的形象，本来会从坟墓里向他们走出来；但是，在对这一精神的敬拜、在对这一形象的直观的享受旁边，本来还会立着对这一形象的生命的怀念，这个崇高的精神本来会始终在它那已经消逝的存在上拥有自己的对立面；而它出现在想象力面前，本来会与一种渴望相连，这渴望所标示的本来只是宗教的需要，可是教团本来还是没有一个属于自己的上帝。

en: For beauty, for divinity, the image lacked life; the divine in the community of love, this life, lacked image and shape.

But in the resurrected one and then in the one raised up to heaven, the image found life again, and love found the presentation of its oneness; in this remarriage of spirit and body the opposition of the living and the dead has vanished and has united itself in one God; the longing of love has found itself as a living being and can now enjoy itself, whose veneration is now the religion of the congregation; the need of religion finds its satisfaction in this resurrected Jesus, in this love that has taken shape.

The contemplation of Jesus's resurrection as an occurrence is the standpoint of the historian, who has nothing to do with religion, belief or unbelief in it, as mere actuality without the interest of religion, is a matter of the understanding, whose activity, the fixation of objectivity, is precisely the death of religion, and to appeal to it means to abstract from religion.

But of course the understanding seems to have a right to have a say, since the objective side of the God is not merely a shape of love, but subsists for itself and claims a place as an actuality in the world of actualities.

And therefore it is hard to hold fast to the religious side of the resurrected Jesus, to the love that has taken shape in its beauty; for only through an apotheosis has he become God, his divinity is a deification of one who is also present as something actual; he had lived as a human individual, had died on the cross and been buried.

This blemish of humanity is something entirely different from the shape that is proper to the God; the objective element of the God, his shape, is objective only to the extent that it is merely the presentation of the love that unites the congregation, merely the pure opposition of that love, and contains nothing that would not itself be in love, though here only as something opposed, nothing that would not at the same time be feeling.

Thus, however, there is added to the image of the resurrected one, to the union that has become essence, still other accessory being, something fully objective, individual, which is to be paired with love, but as something individual, as something opposed, is to remain fixed, fixed for the understanding, which is thereby an actuality that always hangs on the deified one like lead on his feet and pulls him down to the earth; whereas [after all] the God ought to hover in the middle between the heaven's infinite and boundless and the earth, this gathering of pure limitations.
It cannot be got out of the soul, the twofoldness of the natures.

As Heracles through the pyre, so the deified one too has raised himself up to hero only through a grave; but there the altars are consecrated to shaped bravery, [to] the hero who has become a god, who no longer fights or serves, alone, while here [by contrast] not to the hero alone; not the risen one alone is the salvation of sinners and the rapture of their faith; the one who teaches and walks about and hangs on the cross is also worshipped.
It is this monstrous combination over which for so many centuries millions of God-seeking souls have struggled and tormented themselves.
zh: 对于美、对于神性来说，形象缺少的是生命；而爱的共同体中的神性，这生命，缺少的是形象和形态。
但在复活者身上、接着又在升天者身上，形象重新找到了生命，爱也找到了自身合一的呈现；在精神与身体的这次重新联姻中，生者与死者的对立已经消失，并在一个上帝里结合了起来；爱的渴念已经找到自身是一个活生生的存在，如今能够享受自身了，而对它的敬拜如今就是教团的宗教；宗教的需要在这个复活的耶稣身上、在这成形的爱里得到了满足。
把耶稣的复活当作一桩事件来考察，这是历史研究者的立足点，他与宗教毫无关系，对这种作为纯粹现实性、没有宗教旨趣的复活的信或不信，是知性的事，而知性的活动，即对客观性的固定化，恰恰就是宗教的死，援引知性就等于从宗教里抽身出来。
但知性看来确实有权利插话，因为上帝身上的客观一面并不只是爱的一种形态，而是自为地持存着，并且作为一种现实性在诸现实性的世界里占有一个位置。
所以，要牢牢把握住复活了的耶稣的宗教一面，把握住成形的爱在其美中的样子，是很难的；因为他只是通过一次神化才成为上帝，他的神性是对一个同样作为现实者而现成存在的东西的神格化；他曾作为一个人类个体活着，死在十字架上，并被埋葬。
人性的这个瑕疵，与上帝本有的形态完全是另一回事；上帝身上的客观东西，他的形态，只在这样的限度内是客观的，即它只是把教团结合起来的爱的呈现，只是这爱的纯粹对立，并且不包含任何本身不在爱里的东西——不过在这里只是作为被对立者——也不包含任何不同时是感受的东西。
可这样一来，在复活者的形象上、在已变成本质的结合上，又加上了别的附属存在，完全客观的、个体的东西，它应当与爱配成一对，但作为个体的、作为被对立者，却要固定下来，为知性所固定，它因此是一种现实性，始终像脚上的铅一样挂在那被神化者身上，把他拽向大地；而[要知道]上帝本该悬在天的无限者、无限制者与大地——这一大堆纯粹限制的集合——的中间。
这两种本性的二重性，是无法从灵魂里清除掉的。
就像赫拉克勒斯经过火葬堆那样，被神化者也同样只是经过一座坟墓才升为英雄；但在那里，祭坛是献给成形的勇敢的，[是]只献给那位已变成神、不再战斗也不再服侍的英雄的，祈祷也是向他献上的；在这里[相反]，祭坛和祈祷却不是只献给英雄；不只是复活者是罪人的得救和他们信仰的狂喜；那教导人的、四处行走的、挂在十字架上的，也受到敬拜。
正是这个骇人的组合，多少世纪以来，千百万寻求上帝的灵魂为它挣扎过、受尽折磨。

en: It is not the servant's shape, humiliation itself, at which the drive toward religion would take offense as the veil of the divine, if actuality contented itself with being a veil and passing away; but in this way it is to belong firmly and permanently to the God, on and in him, as his essence, and individuality is to be the object of adoration; and the veil of actuality stripped off in the grave has risen up again out of the grave and has attached itself to the one risen as God.
This sad need of the congregation for something actual is deeply connected with its spirit and with its spirit's fate.

Their love, which brings every shape of life to the consciousness of an object and thereby despises it, had indeed recognized itself as shaped in the risen one; but he was not merely love for them; for since their love, cut off from the world, did not present itself in the development of life, nor in life's beautiful relations and in the cultivation of natural relations, since love was to be love and not to live, some criterion of the knowledge of it had to be present for the possibility of mutual belief in it.

Because love did not itself establish the thoroughgoing union, another bond was needed that linked the congregation together and in which it would at the same time find the certainty of the love of all; it had to recognize itself in an actuality.
This was now the sameness of faith, the sameness of having received a doctrine, of having a common master and teacher.
This is a distinctive side of the spirit of the congregation, that the divine, the element uniting it, has for it the form of something given.
Nothing is given to the spirit, to life; what it has received, that it has itself become, that has so passed over into it that it is now a modification of it, that it is its life.

But in the lifelessness of the love of the congregation, the spirit of their love remained so poor, felt itself so empty, that it could not recognize the spirit that spoke to it fully within itself, not as living within itself, and remained foreign to it.

A linking with a spirit that is foreign and felt as foreign is consciousness of dependence on it; since the love of the congregation had on the one hand overleapt itself by extending itself to a whole assembly of human beings, and therefore on the other hand became indeed full in ideal content but lost in life, the unfulfilled ideal of love was a positive for it, it recognized it as opposed to itself and [itself] as dependent on it; in its spirit lay the consciousness of discipleship and of a lord and master; its spirit was not completely presented in the love that has taken shape; the side of it, to have received and to learn and to stand lower than the master, found its presentation only in the shape of love when at the same time an actuality was linked with it that stood over against the congregation.

This higher opposed element is not the sublimity of the God, which the latter necessarily has because in him the individual does not recognize himself as equal to him, but rather the whole spirit of the united all is contained in him, - but it is a positive, objective element that has as much of the foreign, of domination, in itself as there is dependence in the spirit of the congregation.

In this community of dependence, of being a community through a founder, in this intermixture of something historical, actual into its life, the congregation recognized its real bond, the security of the union, which in the lifeless love could not come to feeling.
zh: 宗教的冲动所抵触的，并不是奴仆的形态、屈辱本身，并不是作为神性外壳的它，只要现实性满足于只当一层外壳并转瞬即逝；但照这样，它却应当牢固而持久地附着于上帝、在上帝之中，属于他的本质，而个体性应当成为崇拜的对象；而那在坟墓里被脱下的现实性外壳，又从坟墓里升了上来，附在了那位作为上帝而复活者的身上。
教团这种对一个现实之物的可悲需要，与它的精神以及这精神的命运深深联系在一起。
他们的爱把每一种生命形态都带进对一个对象的意识，并因此蔑视它，这种爱在复活者身上固然认出了自己是成形的；但对他们来说，他并不只是爱；因为他们的爱既然与世界隔绝，既不在生命的发展中呈现自己，也不在生命那些美好的关系和自然关系的培育中呈现自己，既然爱应当只是爱而不应当生活，那么为了彼此相信这爱是可能的，就必须有某种认识这爱的标准存在。
因为爱本身并没有建立起贯穿一切的结合，所以就需要另一条纽带，把教团联结起来，教团在其中同时能找到所有人的爱的确定性；它必须在一个现实性里认出自己。
这个现实之物就是信仰上的相同，就是都领受了一种学说、都有一位共同的师傅和教师的相同。
教团精神有一个突出的方面，就是那神性的东西、那把它结合起来的东西，对它来说具有一种被给予之物的形式。
对精神、对生命，没有什么东西是被给予的；它领受到了什么，它自己就变成了那个东西，那东西已经这样进入它之中，以致它如今是这精神的一个变形，以致它就是这精神的生命。
但在教团之爱的无生命状态里，他们爱的精神始终那么贫乏，感到那么空虚，以致它无法把那个向它说话的精神完整地、活生生地认作在自身之内，并且对它一直是陌生的。

与一个陌生的、被感受为陌生的精神相联结，就是意识到自己依赖于它；教团的爱一方面由于把自己扩展到整整一群人身上而跳过了自身，因此另一方面在理想的内容上固然变得充实，在生命上却有所丧失，于是那未被满足的爱的理想对教团来说就是一个实证的东西，它把这理想认作与自身相对立，并把自身认作依赖于它；在它的精神里，有着门徒身份和有一位主与师傅的意识；它的精神并没有在成形的爱里得到完整呈现；它身上那一面，即领受过、学习过、并且比师傅站得更低，只有在爱的形态里，并且当同时有一种现实性与这爱相联结、而这现实性与教团相对而立的时候，才找到自己的呈现。
这个更高的对立物并不是上帝的崇高，上帝必然具有这种崇高，因为在他里面，个体并不把自己认作与他相等，而是他里面包含着联合起来的全体的整个精神，——相反，它是一个实证的、客观的东西，它自身中有多少陌生的东西、多少支配，教团的精神中就有多少依赖。
在这种依赖的共同体里，在这种通过一位创立者而存在的共同体里，在这种把历史的、现实的东西混进它生命里的做法中，教团认出了自己真正的纽带，认出了结合的安全感——这种安全感在无生命的爱里是无法达到感受的。

en: This is the point at which the congregation, which in the love that keeps itself unmixed outside all covenant with the world seemed to have escaped all fate, was seized by it, but by a fate whose center was the extension of the love that flees all relations to a congregation, a fate that on the one hand developed all the more in the very extension of the congregation and on the other hand through this extension increasingly met with the fate of the world, both by unconsciously taking up many sides of it into itself and by struggling against it, becoming ever more impure.
zh: 这就是那个点：教团在那与世界的任何盟约之外保持自身不混杂的爱里，似乎已经逃过了一切命运，却在这里被命运抓住了——不过是被一种命运抓住，这种命运的中心，是把那逃避一切关系的爱扩展到教团上去；这种命运一方面在教团自身的扩展中越发发展起来，另一方面又通过这种扩展越来越与世界的命运碰在一起，既不知不觉地把世界命运的许多方面纳入自身，又与之抗争，从而越来越不纯净。

en: The ungodly objective element, for which adoration is also demanded, never becomes a divine one through all the splendor that shines around it.
zh: 那非神性的客观东西，尽管人们也要求对它加以崇拜，却绝不会因为环绕在它周围的一切光辉而变成一个神性的东西。

en: To be sure, heavenly appearances also surround the human being Jesus; higher beings are busy around his birth; he himself is once transfigured into a radiant shape of light.
But even these forms of the heavenly are only outside the actual, and the more divine beings around the individual serve only to make the contrast stand out all the more.

Even less than such a passing nimbus can the activities that are regarded as divine and come out of him himself raise him into the higher shape; the miracles, which do not merely hover around him but proceed from his inner power, seem attributes worthy of a god, seem to characterize a god; in them the divine seems most intimately united with the objective, and thus the harsh opposition and mere linking of opposed elements seem here to fall away; those miraculous effects the human being accomplishes, he and the divine seem inseparable.
But the closer the linking is, which nevertheless does not become a union, the more harshly the unnaturalness of the linked opposites strikes the eye.
zh: 诚然，耶稣这个人周围也有天上的现象；他降生时有更高的存在者在忙碌；他自己也曾一度被变形为光辉的形态。
但这些天上的形式也只在现实之物之外，而围绕这个个体的那些更神性的存在者，只是为了让这对比更加刺眼。

比起这种转瞬即逝的光晕，那些被视为神性的、并且从他自身中出来的活动，更不能把他提升到更高的形态里去；那些奇迹并不只是在他周围盘旋，而是从他的内在力量中产生出来，它们看上去是配得上一位上帝的属性，能刻画出一位上帝；在它们里面，神性的东西似乎最亲密地与客观的东西结合在一起，于是那种生硬的对立、以及把对立者仅仅联结起来的做法，在这里似乎就消失了；那些神奇的作用是这个人做出来的，他和神性的东西看来不可分离。
可是，这联结越是紧密，它却毕竟不会成为结合，那些被联结起来的对立者的不自然，就越发刺眼地显现出来。

en: In the miracle as an action, a connection of cause and effect is given to the understanding and the domain of its concepts is acknowledged; but at the same time its domain is thereby destroyed, in that the cause is not something as determinate as the effect, but is supposed to be something infinite; since the connection of cause and effect in the understanding is the sameness of determinateness, their opposition only this, that in the one this determinateness is activity, in the other passivity, — here, however, in the action itself an infinite, with infinite activity, is at the same time supposed to have a most limited effect.
Not the sublation of the domain of the understanding, but that it is at the same time posited and sublated, is what is unnatural.
Just as, on the one hand, the positing of an infinite cause contradicts the positing of a finite effect, so the infinite equally cancels the determinate effect.

There, viewed from the standpoint of the understanding, the infinite is only a negative, the indeterminate, to which something determinate is attached; here, from the side of the infinite as something that is, it is a spirit that acts, and the determinateness of the effect of a spirit is its negative side; only from another standpoint, in comparison, can its action appear determinate; in itself, according to its being, it is the sublation of a determinateness and in itself infinite.
zh: 在作为行动的奇迹里，知性被给予了一个原因和结果的关联，它的概念的领域也得到了承认；但同时它的领域又被这样摧毁：原因并不像结果那样是一个如此确定的东西，而应当是一个无限者；因为在知性里原因和结果的关联就是规定性的相同，它们的对立只在于，在其中一个里这种规定性是能动，在另一个里是受动，——而在这里，在行动本身里，一个具有无限能动的无限者却同时应当有一个极其有限的结果。
不自然的不是知性领域遭到扬弃，而是它同时被设定又被扬弃。
正如一方面设定一个无限的原因与设定一个有限的结果相矛盾，无限者也同样扬弃那确定的结果。
在那里，从知性的观点来看，无限者只是一个否定性的东西、那个不确定者，一个确定的东西被接在它上面；而在这里，从作为存在者的无限者这一方面来看，它是一个起作用的精神，一个精神的结果的规定性就是它否定的一面；只有从比较中的另一个观点出发，它的行动才能显得是确定的，而自在、就它的存在而言，它是对一种规定性的扬弃，并且在自身中是无限的。

en: When a god acts, it is only from spirit to spirit; the activity presupposes an object on which it is exercised; but the effect of the spirit is the sublation of that object.

The going-forth of the divine is only a development, that it, in sublating the opposite, presents itself in the union; but in the miracles the spirit appears as acting on bodies, [and then] the cause would not be a formed spirit whose form, considered merely in its opposition, could as body enter, equal to another and opposable to it, into the connection of cause and effect; this connection would be a community of the spirit, which is spirit only insofar as it has nothing in common with the body, and of the body, which is body because it has nothing in common with the spirit, but spirit and body have nothing in common; they are absolute opposites.

Their union, in which their opposition ceases, is a life, i.e. formed spirit; and when this acts as something divine, undivided, its doing is a marriage with kindred essence, with the divine, and a generation, a development of something new, of the presentation of their union; but insofar as the spirit acts in another, opposed form as something hostile, dominating, it has forgotten its divinity.
Miracles are therefore the presentation of the most ungodly, because they are the most unnatural and contain, bound together, the hardest opposition of spirit and body in all its monstrous crudeness.
Divine doing is the restoration and presentation of unity; miracle, the utmost tearing-apart.

The expectation that has been stirred up — to raise to divinity, through miraculous activities of this actual being, the actuality associated with the transfigured Jesus exalted to a god — is therefore so far from being fulfilled that it rather increases all the more the harshness of this addition of something actual.

Yet it is that much greater for us than for the members of the first Christian congregation, by as much more understanding as we have than they, who, breathed upon by the Oriental spirit, had completed the separation of spirit and body less fully and had delivered less to the understanding as objects.
Where we cognize determinate actuality, historical objectivity with the understanding, there is often spirit for them; and where we posit only pure spirit, there it is still embodied for them.

Of the latter kind of view, the form in which they grasp what we call immortality, namely the immortality of the soul, is an example; it appears to them as a resurrection of the body; both views are the extremes between which the Greek spirit [stands]; the one is the extreme of reason, which sets a soul, a negative as against all understanding, and its object, the dead body, over against each other, the other is the extreme of, so to speak, a positive capacity of reason, which posits the body as living while at the same time it assumed it to be dead; whereas for the Greeks body and soul remain in one living form, in the two extremes, by contrast, death is a separation of body and soul, and in the one the body is nothing more to the soul, in the other the body is something that persists even without life.

In other matters, where we cognize only with the understanding something actual or — which amounts to the same — some alien spirit, the first Christians mix in their own spirit; in the writings of the Jews we see past histories, individual situations and the former spirit of men, in the Jewish acts of worship a commanded doing whose spirit, purpose and thoughts no longer are for us and no longer have any truth; for them all this still had truth and spirit, but their truth, their spirit — they did not let it become objective.

The spirit which they give to passages of the prophets and of other Jewish books is, in their sense, neither — with regard to the prophets — the opinion of finding in them predictions of actualities, nor, on their side, the application to actuality.
It is an uncertain, formless hovering between actuality and spirit; on the one hand, in actuality only the spirit is considered, on the other hand actuality itself as such is present, but not fixed.

To give an example, John (12, 14 ff.) relates to the circumstance that Jesus rode into Jerusalem on a donkey an expression of the prophet, whose inspiration saw such a procession, [and] John lets it find its truth in the procession of Jesus.

The proofs that similar passages of the Jewish books are in part cited, in themselves, incorrectly against the literal sense of the original text, in part explained against their sense, which they receive through their context, in part refer to quite other actualities, to circumstances and men contemporary with the prophets, in part are merely isolated inspiration of the prophets, — all these proofs hit only the actuality of the relation which the apostles set up between them and the circumstances of Jesus' life, not their truth and spirit, just as little as their truth is visible in the strict objective assumption that the actual words and visions of the prophets were the earlier expression of later actualities.

The spirit of the relation which Christ's friends find between the visions of the prophets and the events of Jesus would be conceived too weakly if it were placed merely in the comparison of similarity of situations, in a comparison such as [that by which] we often add to the presentation of a situation the definite expression of old writers.

In the example cited above, John says expressly that Jesus' friends recognized these relations only after Jesus had been glorified, after the spirit had come upon them; had John seen in this relation a mere fancy, a mere similarity of different things, this remark would not have been needed; but as it is, in the spirit that vision of the prophet and this circumstance in an action of Jesus are one; and since the relation is only in the spirit, the objective view of it as a concurrence of actual things, of individual things, falls away.
This spirit, which fixes the actual just as little, or turns it into something indeterminate, and cognizes in it nothing individual but something spiritual, is especially also [to be found in] John

11, 51 visible, where John, in connection with the maxim of Caiaphas and its application, that it is better that one man die for the people than that the whole come into danger, reminds [us] that Caiaphas did not speak this for himself as an individual, but as high priest in prophetic inspiration (πϱοεϕήτευσεν).

What we would perhaps regard from the standpoint of an instrument of divine providence, in that John saw something filled by the spirit, since the character of the view of Jesus and his friends could not be more opposed to anything than to the standpoint of taking everything as machine, tool, instrument, but was rather the highest faith in spirit; and where one sees a unity of the concurrence of actions which, taken singly for themselves, lack this unity, the intention of the whole of the effect, and regards these actions (like those of Caiaphas) as subjected to it, ruled and guided by it without consciousness in their relation to the unity, as actualities and instruments, there John sees unity of the spirit and, in this action itself, the spirit of the whole effect acting; he speaks of Caiaphas as himself filled by the spirit in which the necessity of Jesus' fate lay.
zh: 当一个神起作用时，这只是从精神到精神；作用以一个它施加于其上的对象为前提；但精神的结果就是对这对象的扬弃。

神性者的走出只是一种发展，即它在扬弃对立者时把自身展示在结合里；但在奇迹里，精神显现为作用于身体，那样原因就不会是一个有形态的精神，因为这样一种精神的形态若只在它的对立中来看，作为身体本可以作为一个与另一个相等、并可与另一个相对立的东西进入原因和结果的关联；这种关联就会是精神与身体的一种共同体，而这个精神之所以是精神，只因为它与身体没有任何共同之处，这个身体之所以是身体，只因为它与精神没有任何共同之处，但精神和身体没有任何共同之处；它们是绝对对立的东西。
它们的结合——在结合中它们的对立停止了——是一种生命，即有形态的精神；当这个精神作为神性的、不可分离的东西起作用时，它的作为就是一种与同类本质、与神性者的婚配，并且是新的东西的产生和发展，是对它们的结合的展示；但就精神在另一种对立的形态中作为敌对的、统治性的东西起作用而言，它就忘记了自己的神性。
奇迹因此是最不神圣者的展示，因为它们是最不自然的，并且把精神和身体最坚硬的对立连同它全部骇人的粗野一并联结着包含在内。
神性的行动是统一的重建和展示；奇迹则是极端的撕裂。
因此，那个被激发起来的期待——即通过这个现实者的奇迹般的活动，把与那位得了荣耀、被提升为神的耶稣联系在一起的现实性提升到神性——非但没有得到满足，反倒更加增强了这种把一个现实者附加上的生硬。
不过，它对我们来说要比对最初基督教教团的成员来说大得多，正如我们的知性比他们的更多；他们受东方精神的吹拂，把精神和身体的分离完成得不够彻底，交给知性作为对象的东西也更少。
凡是我们用知性认识确定的现实性、历史客观性的地方，在他们那里往往就是精神；而凡是我们只设定纯粹精神的地方，这精神在他们那里还是具有身体的。

后一种观点的一个例子，就是他们用来把握我们称之为不死、而且是灵魂不死的那种东西的形式；它在他们那里显现为肉体的复活；这两种观点是希腊精神处于其间的两个极端；前一个是对立起灵魂——一个与一切知性相对立的否定性东西——及其对象即死去的身体的理性之极端，后一个可以说是理性的另一种肯定能力的极端，这种能力把身体设定为活的，同时却又把它当作死的；而对于希腊人来说，肉体和灵魂停留在一种活生生的形态里，在这两个极端里，死亡却是肉体和灵魂的分离，在一个极端里肉体对灵魂来说什么也不是了，在另一个极端里肉体即使没有生命也仍然留存。

在另一些事情上，我们只用知性去认识某种现实的东西，或者——这两者是一回事——去认识某种陌生的精神，这时最初的基督徒就把自己的精神掺和进去；在犹太人的书里我们看到的是一段段过去的历史、一个个个别的处境和人们曾经有过的精神，在犹太人的礼拜行动中看到的是被命令的行为，这种行为的精神、目的和思想对于我们来说已经不复存在，不再有任何真理；而对他们来说，这一切还曾具有真理和精神，但那是他们的真理、他们的精神，他们并没有让它成为客观的。
他们赋予先知书和其他犹太书中的段落的那种精神，在他们的意思里，既不是就先知而言要在其中找到关于现实性的预言的看法，也不是他们这边对现实性的应用。
这是一种在现实性和精神之间不确定的、无形态的飘浮；一方面，在现实性中只被考察到精神，另一方面，现实性本身作为这样的东西是现成的，却没有被固定下来。
举一个例子：约翰（12, 14 ff.）把先知的一句话联系到耶稣骑着一头驴进入耶路撒冷这件事上；那位先知的灵感曾看见这样一支队伍，约翰就让这句话在耶稣的这支队伍里找到它的真理。

这些证明——即犹太书中类似的段落，一部分自在地就是违背原文的字面意义被引用的，一部分是违背它们通过上下文获得的含义而被解释的，一部分涉及完全另一些现实性、涉及与先知同时代的情况和人，一部分只是先知孤立的灵感——所有这些证明只击中使徒在它们和耶稣的生活境况之间建立起来的那种关系的现实性，而没有击中它们的真理和精神；正如它们的真理也不可能在那种严格客观的假定中显现出来，即先知实际说过的话和实际看见的异象是后来的现实性的较早表达。
基督的朋友们在先知的异象和耶稣的事件之间发现的那种关系的精神，如果只被放在对种种处境相似性的比较里，被放在这样一种比较里——就像我们常常给对某个处境的描述附上古代作家的某个确定说法那样——那就被理解得太弱了。
在上面所举的例子中，约翰明确地说，耶稣的朋友们是在耶稣得了荣耀、在精神降临到他们身上之后，才认识到这些关系的；如果约翰在这种关系里看到的只是一种突然的念头、不同事物的一种单纯相似，那么这一说明本来就不需要；但情形既然如此，在精神里，先知的那个异象和耶稣某次行动中的这个情况就是一回事；而由于这种关系只在精神里，把它看作种种现实的东西、种种个别的东西的凑合的那种客观观点就消失了。
这种精神对现实的东西同样不予固定，或者把它变成一种不确定的东西，并且在其中认识到的不是任何个别的东西，而是一种精神性的东西，它尤其还见于约翰
11, 51 处可以看到：约翰在谈到该亚法的准则及其运用——即一个人为民众而死，总比整个民众陷入危险要好——时提醒说，该亚法说这话并不是以个人的身份为自己说的，而是作为大祭司在预言的灵感中说的（πϱοεϕήτευσεν）。

我们也许会从上帝护佑的一个工具这一观点去看的东西，约翰在其中看到的却是一种被精神充满的东西，因为耶稣和他的朋友们的观点的性质，不可能与那种把一切都当作机器、工具、器具的观点更加对立，它反倒是对于精神的最高信仰；而凡是人们看到一种行动的凑合的统一的地方——这些行动单个自为地看就缺少这种统一，缺少整个结果的意图——并且把这些行动（比如该亚法的行动）看作服从于它、被它无意识地在与统一的关系中支配和引导的现实性和工具的地方，约翰就看到精神的统一，并且在这种行动本身中看到整个结果的精神在行动；他谈该亚法时，说他自己就被那种精神所充满，而耶稣命运中的必然性就在这种精神里。

en: Thus, too, seen with the soul of the apostles, the miracles lose something of the harshness which the opposition of spirit and body in them has for us, since it is evident that those men lacked the European understanding, which so strips all spirit from what enters consciousness and fixes it into absolute objectivities, into actualities absolutely opposed to spirit, that their cognition is rather an indeterminate hovering between actuality and spirit, which indeed still separated the two, but did not separate them so irrevocably, and moreover did not merge into pure nature, but already gave the clear opposition itself, which with further development had to become a pairing of the living and the dead, of the divine and the actual, which through the placing of the actual Jesus alongside the transfigured, the one become God, showed satisfaction to the deepest drive toward religion, but did not grant it, and made it into an infinite, inextinguishable and unappeased longing; for to the longing, in its highest enthusiasm, in the raptures of the most finely organized souls breathing the highest love, there always stands opposed the individual, something objective, personal, after union with which all the depths of their beautiful feelings languished, but which union, because it is an individual, is eternally impossible, since it always remains over against them, eternally in their consciousness, and never lets religion become complete life.
zh: 所以，用使徒的灵魂来看，奇迹也失去了精神和身体的对立在我们这里所具有的那种生硬，因为可以看到，他们缺少欧洲式的知性，这种知性把一切精神都从进入意识的东西里抽走，把它固定为绝对的客观性、固定为与精神绝对对立的现实性；他们的认识倒毋宁是一种在现实性和精神之间不确定的飘浮，这种飘浮虽然还把两者分开，却没有把它们分得那么不可挽回，而且终究没有合为纯粹的自然，反倒是已经给出了那种清晰的对立，这种对立在进一步发展时必然会变成活的东西与死的东西、神性的东西与现实的东西的配对，而这个配对通过把现实的耶稣与得了荣耀的、变成了神的耶稣并列在一起，向最深的宗教冲动显示出了满足，却没有给予满足，反而把它变成了无限的、不可磨灭的、无法平息的热望；因为对于这种热望来说，在它最高的狂热中、在最精细地组织起来的、呼吸着最高爱的灵魂的沉醉中，总是有那个个体，一个客观的、人格性的东西与它相对而立，而他们美好感受的一切深处都在渴望着与这个个体的结合，但这种结合，因为它是一个个体，永远是不可能的，因为它始终在他们对面，永远留在他们的意识里，使宗教永远不能成为完整的生命。

en: In all forms of the Christian religion that have developed in the continuing fate of time, this fundamental character of opposition rests in the divine, which is supposed to be present only in consciousness, never in life — from the rapturous unions of the enthusiast, who renounces all manifoldness of life, even the purest, in which the spirit enjoys itself, and is conscious only of God, and thus could remove the opposition of personality only in death, up to the actuality of the most manifold consciousness, of the union with the fate of the world and of God's opposition to it — either the felt opposition in all actions and expressions of life, which purchase their legitimacy through the feeling of the servitude and nullity of their opposition, as in the Catholic church, or God's opposition in mere more or less devout thoughts, as in the Protestant church — either the opposition of a hating God to life, as a disgrace and a crime, in some sects of the same, or of a benevolent [God] to life and its joys, as altogether something received, benefits and gifts from him, as altogether actuality, into which then also the form of spirit hovering above it is drawn down, in the idea of a divine man, of the prophets, etc., to historical objective view —: between these extremes of the manifold or diminished consciousness of friendship, of hatred, or of indifference toward the world, between these extremes which lie within the opposition of God and the world, of the divine and of life, the Christian church has run the circle forwards and backwards, but it is against its essential character to find rest in an impersonal living beauty; and it is its fate that church and state, divine service and life, piety and virtue, spiritual and worldly doing can never melt together into one.
zh: 在基督教宗教的一切形式里——这些形式是在时间不断前行的命运中发展出来的——对立的这一基本特征都栖息于神性者之中，而这个神性者应当只在意识里、从不在生命里在场，——从狂热者的那些令人沉醉的结合，即他弃绝生命的一切杂多、也包括最纯粹的杂多（在那种杂多里精神享受自身），并且只意识到上帝，因而只有在死亡中才能去掉人格性的对立，一直到最杂多的意识的现实性、与世界命运的结合以及上帝对世界命运的对立，——要么是在一切行动和生命表现中感受到的那种对立，这类行动和生命表现以自己的对立所带有的奴役性和虚无性的感受来换取自己的合法性，如同在天主教会里那样，要么是在仅仅或多或少虔诚的思想中上帝的对立，如同在新教教会里那样，——要么是某些教派中一个仇恨生命的上帝与生命相对立，把它当作耻辱和罪行，要么是一个仁慈的上帝与生命及其欢乐相对立，把这一切都当作接受来的东西、当作他的恩惠和礼物，当作纯粹的现实性，于是连那悬浮在它之上的精神形式，也在一个神性的人、先知等等的观念中被拉低为历史的客观观点——：在这些极端之间，即在对世界的友谊、仇恨或漠不关心的杂多的或减少了的意识之间，在这些处于上帝与世界、神性者与生命的对立之内的极端之间，基督教会向前和向后跑完了这个圆圈，但要在一种非人格的、活生生的美中找到安宁，却是违背它的本质特征的；而它的命运就是：教会与国家、礼拜与生命、虔诚与美德、宗教的作为与世俗的作为，永远不能融而为一。
